items.headline: Governor Ron DeSantis announces $60 million in cancer innovation awards and opens $70 million application cycle
items.summary: Florida announced $60 million in awards through the 2025-26 Florida Cancer Innovation Fund and opened the 2026-27 application cycle with $70 million available for new awards.
items.source: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida

items.headline: Florida regulators approve additional power for JEA's $1.57 billion, 675-megawatt natural-gas plant
items.summary: The Florida Public Service Commission approved JEA's need for additional power to support construction of a combined-cycle plant at the former St. Johns River Power Park site. Officials said the approval keeps the project on schedule to begin operations in 2031.

items.headline: SwRI develops dynamic framework to better predict wildfires
items.summary: Southwest Research Institute announced a framework for early wildfire detection that combines datasets, remote sensing and real-time modeling. The institute said the tool can identify risk factors up to 30 days before a wildfire outbreak.

items.headline: NYC Health Department detects first person with West Nile virus in 2026
items.summary: New York City's Health Department reported the first city resident with West Nile virus this year. The department said it intensified mosquito surveillance and expanded control efforts after virus-positive mosquitoes were detected across all five boroughs.
items.source: New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

items.headline: Appellate court reverses judgment in NYCERS accidental-disability retirement case
items.summary: New York's Appellate Division, Second Department reversed a lower-court judgment and dismissed a petition challenging the New York City Employees' Retirement System's denial of accidental-disability retirement benefits. The court held that NYCERS had a rational basis for its determination.
items.entityName: New York City Employees' Retirement System
items.source: New York State Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department

items.headline: Summit County advises Medicaid clients about possible work requirement
items.summary: Summit County said the Ohio Department of Medicaid is mailing notices to some Group VIII Medicaid enrollees about federal work requirements scheduled to begin January 1, 2027. The release said recipients should review the notices and respond by the listed deadlines.

items.headline: Bexar County approves 10-year tax break for H-E-B East Side expansion
items.summary: Bexar County commissioners approved a 10-year property-tax abatement for H-E-B's East Side expansion. County officials estimate the agreement will reduce the company's county property-tax bill by more than $15 million while H-E-B has projected 720 new jobs.

items.headline: Cleveland City Council considers more than $1.1 million in emergency stadium repairs
items.summary: Cleveland City Council was set to hear legislation authorizing more than $1.1 million in emergency repairs to Huntington Bank Field. The Browns organization had already made most of the repairs and was seeking reimbursement from the city.

items.headline: HHSC hosts Rural Texas Strong public forum in Big Spring
items.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission hosted a public forum in Big Spring to provide information and gather feedback on the Rural Texas Strong plan. The five-year plan is supported by approximately $1.4 billion in federal funding and will distribute assistance through six initiatives for rural communities.
items.entityName: Texas Health and Human Services Commission

items.headline: North Carolina invests in child care training to combat shortages
items.summary: The North Carolina General Assembly directed $1.5 million in one-time state-budget funding to expand free child-care worker training academies statewide. The funding also supports retention stipends for academy graduates who remain employed for at least one year.
